paras: The rumored lynching of Homer and Oliver Hart was a report, sent from Detroit on the night of March 4, 1888, that a father and son from Mount Pleasant, Michigan, arrested on a charge of criminally assaulting the son's five-year-old daughter, had been lynched. The rumor came without particulars and was reprinted in papers across the country, some of which headlined it as fact. No confirmation or denial appears in the coverage.

According to an East Saginaw dispatch of March 3, warrants were issued at Mount Pleasant, in Isabella County, on Thursday night for Homer Hart and Oliver Hart of Lincoln township. Both were charged with criminally assaulting Jessie Hart, Oliver's five-year-old daughter. The dispatch alleged that Homer, her 60-year-old grandfather, had assaulted the child four weeks earlier when sent to bring her home from her grandmother's, and that her father had twice done the same in his wife's presence, threatening to kill her if she interfered.
A separate dispatch dated at Mount Pleasant gave the son's name as Oliver A. Hart and said the complaint was made by the child's mother. The men were arrested on Friday, March 2.

On the night of March 4 a Detroit wire stated that it was "rumored here to-night" that the two men had been lynched. The same dispatch explained that there was no telephone connection with Mount Pleasant and that the telegraph office was closed, so particulars were not expected that night. No later dispatch supplying those particulars, naming any participants or describing how the men were said to have died was found.

The coverage contains no report of an inquest, of a trial of the Harts, or of what became of them, and no denial of the rumor. Papers were still printing the rumor unchanged on March 8, and a Bismarck weekly repeated it on March 16 with the lynching placed "in Detroit."

The story reached readers in two stages: first as an arrest for a crime that the Rock Island Daily Argus headed "Can Depravity Bo [Be] More Depraved?", then as a lynching rumor. The Mount Pleasant dispatch, still running in the Fort Worth Weekly Gazette on March 16, called the case "unprecedented in the criminal annals of the country" and the father a "monster of a husband."

Headline writers handled the rumor differently. The Sacramento Daily Record-Union announced "A Brace of Brutes" and "Two Unnatural Creatures Lynched for a Shocking Crime," and the Los Angeles Daily Herald used "Incestuous Parents Lynched," though the text beneath each called the lynching a rumor. Others kept the doubt in the headline: the Indianapolis Journal's "Rumored Lynching of Father and Son," the Omaha Daily Bee's "Reported Lynched" and the St. Paul Daily Globe's "Were They Lynched?" The Rock Island Daily Argus called the men "miscreants," and no paper in the coverage criticized the reported lynching.
None of the reports gives the race of Homer or Oliver Hart.
Whether the lynching took place is unresolved: every text calls it a rumor, while two headlines stated it as fact. The child is named Jessie in both arrest dispatches but "Jennie" in one rumor item.

bases: The only reported violence is a Detroit rumor that the two arrested men had been lynched (A2, A3, A7); no paper confirmed or denied it.

Every report of a killing is a single Detroit rumor that the men 'had been lynched', with no particulars, no named mob and no later confirmation or denial (A2, A3, A7, A13); the accusation that would supply the pretext is well reported (A1, A15), but no killing is established.
The arrest is reported by separate East Saginaw and Mount Pleasant dispatches (A1, A15), but the lynching rests on one Detroit rumor reprinted nationally (A2, A3, A5, A7) and never confirmed.

accounts.label: Arrest dispatches (East Saginaw, Mount Pleasant)
accounts.gist: Warrants were issued at Mount Pleasant for Homer and Oliver Hart on a charge of criminally assaulting Oliver's five-year-old daughter; the complaint came from the child's mother.

accounts.label: Detroit rumor wire
accounts.gist: It was rumored in Detroit on the night of March 4 that the two men, arrested Friday, had been lynched; with no telephone and the telegraph office closed, no particulars were available.

framing.detail: The Sacramento Daily Record-Union headlined the rumor 'A Brace of Brutes. Two Unnatural Creatures Lynched for a Shocking Crime', stating as fact what its text called a rumor.
The Los Angeles Daily Herald ran the rumor as 'Incestuous Parents Lynched'.

The Indianapolis Journal, Omaha Daily Bee, St. Paul Daily Globe and Stark County Democrat headlined it as a rumor or question: 'Rumored Lynching of Father and Son', 'Reported Lynched', 'Were They Lynched?', 'Double Lynching Reported'.
The Rock Island Daily Argus headed the arrest story 'Can Depravity Bo [Be] More Depraved?' and called the men 'miscreants' in its rumor item.

The Fort Worth Weekly Gazette's Mount Pleasant dispatch called the case 'unprecedented in the criminal annals of the country', said there was 'no question of the truth of the complaint' and called Oliver a 'monster of a husband'.

conflicts.note: Three reports, including both arrest dispatches, give Jessie.
The texts under every headline call it a rumor; no report confirms or denies it.
The Bismarck brief appears to have confused the Detroit dateline with the place; the wire placed the men at Mount Pleasant.
